Multiply each entry by -2: -2 times 5 is -10, -2 times 0 is 0, and -2 times -1 is 2. Therefore -2\(\begin{pmatrix}5&0&-1\end{pmatrix}\) = \(\begin{pmatrix}-10&0&2\end{pmatrix}\).

questions.prompt: Find x if 4\(\begin{pmatrix}x&2\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}\) has top-left entry 12.
questions.answer: The top-left entry of 4\(\begin{pmatrix}x&2\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}\) is 4x. We need 4x = 12. Dividing by 4 gives \(x=3\). Therefore \(x=3\).

questions.prompt: A student says -A means take the reciprocal of every entry of A. Diagnose this using \(A=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\0&4\end{pmatrix}\).
questions.answer: The statement is incorrect. The matrix -A is the additive inverse of A, so it is obtained by multiplying every entry by -1. For \(A=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\0&4\end{pmatrix}\), we get -\(A=\begin{pmatrix}-2&1\\0&-4\end{pmatrix}\). Reciprocals would give entries such as 1/2 and 1/4, and the zero entry would not even have a reciprocal. Therefore -A means entrywise negation, not entrywise reciprocal.
